title: "scNotebooks ↔ Workshop Crosswalk"
subtitle: "How our tutorials map to the LatinCells / scNotebooks Jupyter modules"
---

[scNotebooks](https://integrativebioinformatics.github.io/scNotebooks/) is an open, multilingual (English / Spanish / Portuguese) Jupyter-notebook curriculum for single-cell and spatial genomics, developed by the **Integrative Bioinformatics group** in collaboration with the **Human Cell Atlas**, **LatinCells**, and **Wellcome Connecting Sciences**. It runs as 13 modules, each a self-contained `.ipynb` you can open in Google Colab or run locally with their Docker image.

This page maps each of their modules to the corresponding tutorial(s) and lecture(s) in our workshop, so you can use scNotebooks as a parallel-language companion or as a feeder for topics we don't yet cover. Both curricula use **Seurat in R** as the main scRNA-seq toolkit, and both use the same canonical **`ifnb`** dataset for integration teaching.

::: callout-tip
**If you finish our workshop and want more.** The modules in the bottom block of the table — pseudotime, cell–cell communication, multimodal CITE-seq, TCR profiling, spatial transcriptomics, alternative polyadenylation, FAIR data sharing — are topics we **don't** currently cover. scNotebooks is a high-quality entry point for each of them.
:::

## Direct correspondences

The first five scNotebooks modules cover the same workflow as our Tutorials 01–09. Module 10 (Spatial) maps to our Tutorial 12. Module 11 (scATAC) is the ArchR alternative to our Signac-based Tutorial 10.

| scNotebooks module | Workshop equivalent | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Module 01** — Notebooks & databases ([html](https://integrativebioinformatics.github.io/scNotebooks/modules/en/module01/module01.html)) | [Appendix G — Gene-Expression Databases & File Formats](Appendix_G_Databases_FileFormats.html) | We don't reproduce the Jupyter / Colab introduction (Quarto plays that role for our workshop), but we adapted their database tour into a written field guide covering the big-six repositories (GEO, SRA, SCEA, HCA, CELLxGENE, PanglaoDB / CellTypist), expanded with a detailed file-format reference (FASTQ, mtx, h5, fragments.tsv.gz, AnnData, .rds), and a hands-on exploration exercise. |
| **Module 02** — Intro to R + ggplot2 ([html](https://integrativebioinformatics.github.io/scNotebooks/modules/en/module02/module02.html)) | [Appendix D — R Programming](Appendix_D_R_Programming.html) | Their walkthrough is in Colab; ours is a Quarto reference chapter you read alongside RStudio. The R-side topics from Module 02 — lists / matrices / factors as data structures, named vs positional arguments, dplyr verbs, ggplot2 grammar of graphics — are all covered in Appendix D's later sections. |
| **Module 03** — Cell Ranger / raw-seq processing ([html](https://integrativebioinformatics.github.io/scNotebooks/modules/en/module03/module03.html)) | [Talapas Advanced — Raw RNA Cell Ranger](../Exercise_Folder/Talapas_RawData/Tutorial_Talapas_RawData_RNA.html) + [Talapas Advanced — Raw ATAC](../Exercise_Folder/Talapas_RawData/Tutorial_Talapas_RawData_ATAC.html) | We adapted this for **SLURM on Talapas**. The laptop sequence still starts at the filtered Cell Ranger output (so beginners aren't blocked); the Talapas Advanced tutorials walk `cellranger count` and `cellranger-atac count` as batch jobs once you have your own raw FASTQs. |
| **Module 04** — QC, clustering, annotation, functional analysis ([html](https://integrativebioinformatics.github.io/scNotebooks/modules/en/module04/module04.html)) | [Tutorials 01](../Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_01_QC_Preprocessing.html) + [02](../Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_02_DimReduction_Clustering.html) + [03](../Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_03_Markers_Annotation.html) + [07 functional analysis](../Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_07_FunctionalAnalysis.html) + [08 differential abundance](../Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_08_DifferentialAbundance.html) + [09 reference annotation](../Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_09_Reference_Annotation.html) | scNotebooks combines QC + clustering + annotation + GO enrichment + ambient-RNA correction into **one long module**; we split them across four shorter tutorials with paired *Think about it* prompts. Their dataset is **GSE145926** (Liao 2020 COVID-19 BAL fluid, 4 patients); ours is `ifnb`. |
| **Module 05** — Multi-sample integration ([html](https://integrativebioinformatics.github.io/scNotebooks/modules/en/module05/module05.html)) | [Tutorial 04 — Two-Sample Integration](../Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_04_Integration.html) | **Same dataset (`ifnb`)** and **same two methods** (Seurat anchors + Harmony) as ours. They add a quantitative neighborhood-mixing metric we don't yet compute — see [Adopted ideas](#adopted-ideas) below. |

## Topics we don't cover (yet)

Modules 06–13 of scNotebooks extend into territory our workshop currently leaves to outside reading. They're a natural next step.

| scNotebooks module | What it covers | Worth opening? |
|---|---|---|
| **Module 06** — Pseudotime / trajectory ([html](https://integrativebioinformatics.github.io/scNotebooks/modules/en/module06/module06.html)) | Monocle3 trajectory inference, pseudotime ordering, dynamic gene expression | Yes — for any developmental / differentiation study |
| **Module 07** — Cell–cell communication ([html](https://integrativebioinformatics.github.io/scNotebooks/modules/en/module07/module07.html)) | LIANA: ligand–receptor inference, multi-method consensus | Yes — increasingly common in disease / immune work |
| **Module 08** — Multimodal CITE-seq ([html](https://integrativebioinformatics.github.io/scNotebooks/modules/en/module08/module08.html)) | RNA + ADT (antibody-derived tags) joint analysis on CBMC data | Yes — the standard way to add surface-protein resolution to scRNA-seq |
| **Module 09** — TCR profiling ([html](https://integrativebioinformatics.github.io/scNotebooks/modules/en/module09/module09.html)) | T-cell receptor sequencing with V(D)J + transcriptome | Mainly for immunology / vaccine / autoimmunity work |
| **Module 10** — Spatial transcriptomics ([html](https://integrativebioinformatics.github.io/scNotebooks/modules/en/module10/module10.html)) | 10x Visium pipeline in Seurat; spatial deconvolution | Yes — quickly becoming a core technique |
| **Module 11** — scATAC-seq with **ArchR** ([html](https://integrativebioinformatics.github.io/scNotebooks/modules/en/module11/module11.html)) | ArchR pipeline: peak calling, motif enrichment, TF regulators, trajectory | Pairs naturally with our [Tutorial 10 — scATAC-seq with Signac](../Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_10_scATACseq_Signac.html). Same biology, different toolkit (ArchR vs Signac). Read both for breadth. |
| **Module 12** — Alternative polyadenylation ([html](https://integrativebioinformatics.github.io/scNotebooks/modules/en/module12/module12.html)) | SCAPE-APA: detection of poly(A) site usage from scRNA-seq | Specialist; useful if you suspect APA-driven regulation |
| **Module 13** — FAIR data sharing ([html](https://integrativebioinformatics.github.io/scNotebooks/modules/en/module13/module13.html)) | [Lecture 11 — FAIR Principles & Data Sharing](../Lecture_Folder/Lecture_11_FAIR_DataSharing.html) + [Tutorial 13 — FAIR Metadata & Submission](../Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_13_FAIR_Metadata.html) | We adapted Module 13 into a full lecture + a hands-on tutorial that builds a CELLxGENE-conformant metadata sheet, converts the workshop's `ifnb_annotated_final.rds` to AnnData, and generates BioSample/SRA/GEO upload TSVs. |

## Adopted ideas

A few things we picked up from scNotebooks while building our `ifnb`-based laptop sequence:

-   **Same dataset for integration teaching.** scNotebooks Module 05 uses `ifnb` exactly as we do in [Tutorial 04](../Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_04_Integration.html). Independent convergence on the same choice is a good signal that it's the right one for laptop-scale integration.
-   **Per-sample HVGs before integration.** Both curricula split the object by sample and run `NormalizeData` + `FindVariableFeatures` per sample before combining — see Tutorial 04 Step 1.
-   **`SoupX` ambient-RNA correction.** scNotebooks Module 04 walks SoupX in detail; we picked it up as Step 5 of [Tutorial 01](../Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_01_QC_Preprocessing.html) (illustrative since `ifnb`'s filtered-only cache can't run it directly, but the worked recipe is there).
-   **`scDblFinder` doublet detection.** Added as Step 6 of [Tutorial 01](../Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_01_QC_Preprocessing.html), run per sample, with the `scDblFinder.class == "singlet"` filter folded into the QC subset in Step 7.
-   **`miloR` differential abundance.** Added as new [Tutorial 08](../Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_08_DifferentialAbundance.html) — the compositional-shift complement to pseudobulk DE, on the same `ifnb` STIM-vs-CTRL contrast.
-   **`clusterProfiler` functional analysis.** Added as new [Tutorial 07](../Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_07_FunctionalAnalysis.html) — GO over-representation, GSEA, Reactome, and `compareCluster` cross-cell-type comparison on the pseudobulk DE table from Tutorial 06.
-   **Spatial transcriptomics.** Added as new [Tutorial 12](../Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_12_Spatial_Transcriptomics.html) — Visium QC, clustering, spatially variable features, and two-section integration on `stxBrain` (mouse brain anterior + posterior). Different platform (Seurat-Visium vs scNotebooks Module 10's `semla` approach), same conceptual workflow.
-   **Quantitative integration metrics.** scNotebooks computes a per-cluster batch-mixing metric and a neighborhood-mixing score. Our Tutorial 04 uses a **per-cell-type STIM-vs-CTRL ISG score gap** as the over-correction diagnostic (a different but complementary check). Future revision could add a neighborhood-mixing entropy / LISI metric to make the side-by-side method comparison more numerical.

## How to use scNotebooks alongside the workshop

-   **Browse:** the [scNotebooks website](https://integrativebioinformatics.github.io/scNotebooks/) renders every module in three languages with copy-ready code cells.
-   **Run on Colab:** open any `.ipynb` directly in Google Colab — no local install. Their [Colab tutorial](https://github.com/integrativebioinformatics/scNotebooks/blob/main/Tutorial_Open_scNotebooks_Colab.md) walks through the upload step.
-   **Run locally:** their [Docker image](https://github.com/integrativebioinformatics/scNotebooks/blob/main/Tutorial_docker.md) bundles everything.
-   **Read PDFs of pre-run output:** all modules ship as [executed PDFs](https://github.com/integrativebioinformatics/scNotebooks/tree/main/PDF) you can flip through without running anything.
